title: Rigveda 5.23: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.23: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.23 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 335v-336r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>agne̱ saha̍nta̱m ā bha̍ra dyu̱mnasya̍ prā̱sahā̍ ra̱yim | viśvā̱ yaś ca̍rṣa̱ṇīr a̱bhy ā̱3̱̍sā vāje̍ṣu sā̱saha̍t ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>By thy fair splendour's mighty power, O Agni, bring victorious wealth, Wealth that o'ercometh all mankind, and, near us, conquereth in fight.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 335v (numbered 8v by the scribe) (OPenn image 336, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.22.1 ‹pra viśva-sāman atri-vat arca›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 336r (numbered 9r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.23.2 ‹pṛtanāsaham rayim sahasvaḥ ā›. Verse 5.23.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.23.2-4 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 336r
translation.original_text:
2tam a̍gne pṛtanā̱ṣaha̍ṁ ra̱yiṁ sa̍hasva̱ ā bha̍ra | tvaṁ hi sa̱tyo adbhu̍to dā̱tā vāja̍sya̱ goma̍taḥ ||
3viśve̱ hi tvā̍ sa̱joṣa̍so̱ janā̍so vṛ̱ktaba̍rhiṣaḥ | hotā̍ra̱ṁ sadma̍su pri̱yaṁ vyanti̱ vāryā̍ pu̱ru ||
4sa hi ṣmā̍ vi̱śvaca̍rṣaṇir a̱bhimā̍ti̱ saho̍ da̱dhe | agna̍ e̱ṣu kṣaye̱ṣv ā re̱van na̍ḥ śukra dīdihi dyu̱mat pā̍vaka dīdihi ||
translation.text:
2Victorious Agni, bring to us the wealth that vanquisheth in war; For thou art wonderful and true, giver of strength in herds of kine.
3For all the folk with one accord, whose sacred grass is trimmed and strewn, Invite thee to their worship-halls, as a dear Priest, for choicest wealth.
4For he, the God of all men, hath gotten him might that quelleth foes. O Agni, in these homes shine forth, bright God! for our prosperity, shine, Purifier! splendidly.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 336r (numbered 9r by the scribe) (OPenn image 336, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.23.2 ‹pṛtanāsaham rayim sahasvaḥ ā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 336v (numbered 9v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.24.4 ‹-sakhi-bhyaḥ›. Verses 5.23.2-4 end on this page; 5.23.2 begins on fol. 335v (numbered 8v by the scribe).

2tam | agne | pṛtanāsaham | rayim | sahasvaḥ | ā | bhara | tvam | hi | satyaḥ | adbhutaḥ | dātā | vājasya | go--mataḥ
3viśve | hi | tvā | sa-joṣasaḥ | janāsaḥ | vṛkta-barhiṣaḥ | hotāram | sadma-su | priyam | vyanti | vāryā | puru
4saḥ | hi | sma | viśva-carṣaṇiḥ | abhi-māti | sahaḥ | dadhe | agne | eṣu | kṣayeṣu | ā | revat | naḥ | śukra | dīdihi | dyu-mat | pāvaka | dīdihi
